title: Alljoined details ENIGMA model and open EEG datasets for visual neural decoding
summary: Alljoined developed the ENIGMA multi-subject model to reconstruct seen images from non-invasive EEG signals. The architecture uses a unified spatio-temporal backbone with subject alignment layers, supported by the Alljoined-1.6M image-response dataset and the NOVA emotion dataset.
research_notes:
Acquire multi-channel EEG signals from subjects viewing visual stimuli using consumer-grade or laboratory EEG hardware such as a 32-channel wet-electrode cap.

Collect approximately 15 minutes of user-specific EEG calibration data to adapt ENIGMA's shared multi-subject representation to individual brain patterns.

Process raw EEG signals through the spatio-temporal backbone and multi-subject latent alignment layers to project signals into the visual latent space for image reconstruction.

Pre-train neural decoding backbones across multi-subject pools to learn generalized visual representations rather than training separate individual models from scratch.

Deploy lightweight unified spatio-temporal backbones with latent alignment layers to minimize parameter counts and enable local inference without large compute clusters.
